html:
The Romanian peasants' revolt of 1907 was a rising of peasants against landlords and their leaseholders that began in February 1907 at Flămânzi in northern Moldavia and spread across the whole country by March.

Most Romanian peasants worked small plots and rented land from large estates on harsh terms through middlemen, some of them Jewish, so the revolt started with attacks on leaseholders and turned against landlords in general. Peasants burned manor houses and seized grain. The government sent in the army, which shelled villages. Thousands of peasants were killed, though the exact number is disputed. The shock led to land reform after World War I. It inspired the novel Răscoala by Liviu Rebreanu and paintings by Octav Băncilă, and it showed the deep poverty of rural Romania.
